title: Where Did Pipo's Hop Go?
summary: One morning, Pipo the rabbit wakes up and his hop is gone. His friends search everywhere for it, but the one who knows what to do is Grandma.

scenes.text:
One morning, Pipo the rabbit came out of his burrow as usual.

And as usual, he went to do a hop.

But the hop didn't come.

Pipo tried again. He bent his back legs, got ready to spring… and nothing. All that came out was a short little step, like a sleepy snail's.

Nothing hurt. He wasn't ill. His legs just felt heavy, and there was something grey inside him, like a cloud that wouldn't go away.

Pipo sat down in the middle of the meadow, with his ears drooping.

"I've lost my hop," he said quietly.

After a while his friends arrived: Rita the squirrel and Benito the mole.

"What's the matter, Pipo? Your ears are all droopy."

"I've lost my hop."

Rita and Benito looked at each other very seriously.

"Then we'll have to find it," said Rita.

Rita climbed the tallest tree and searched among the branches, in the nests, under every single one of the leaves.

Benito dug a very long tunnel and searched under the ground.

"Down here there are roots, a stone and a very sleepy worm," he shouted from the hole. "But no hop."

"Maybe you've forgotten how to do it," said Rita. "Look, it's easy. Like this: boing!"

And she did a perfect jump.

Benito wanted to show him too. But moles can't jump. Benito got ready, lifted his little paws and fell nose-first into the grass. Bump!

Pipo tried again, watching Rita. He bent his legs. He got ready.

Short little step.

"What if it never comes back?" he asked, in a tiny voice.

Nobody knew what to say.

Then Grandma Rabbit arrived, slowly, with her walking stick made from a twig.

She didn't ask anything. She didn't search for anything. She didn't teach him anything.

She sat down next to Pipo, and stayed there.

A long while passed. A cloud passed, shaped like an ear.

"Mine gets lost sometimes too," Grandma said at last.

"Your hop? What do you do?"

"Nothing. I sit down and wait for it. You don't look for a hop, Pipo. It comes back by itself, when it's ready."

Rita climbed down from the tree. Benito came out of his tunnel. And they sat down too, all four in a row, watching the clouds go by.

They stayed like that all afternoon.

Benito got so relaxed that he fell asleep on the grass. And after a little while he started making a very strange noise, like a teeny-tiny kettle: he was snoring.

Rita covered her mouth. Grandma smiled. And Pipo let out a laugh so big that it shook his whole body.

And as he laughed, without even noticing, he did a little jump.

Small. But real.

"It's back!" shouted Rita.

Pipo looked at his legs. They weren't heavy any more. The grey thing inside had gone very small.

Ever since that day, when a friend in the meadow loses their hop, Pipo knows what to do. He doesn't search for anything. He sits down beside them, and waits with them.
